reasons: The tests were read but not run during this review.
The module description records the bug that was observed before the fix, which is good evidence of intent.

terms.meaning: the scheduler that switches between async tasks so they appear to run together
a point where async code pauses to wait for something, letting other tasks run
a mechanism that collects warnings raised during a block of code
running many similar jobs at once

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and shared setup
sections.what: Brings in asyncio, the cartographer, the schema types, and the stub client. It also marks the tests as async.
sections.why: Gives the concurrency tests the tools they need without calling a real model.
sections.watch_out: The module description explains that a stub which never pauses cannot show this bug, so keep the pausing helper in use.

sections.name: anyio_backend
sections.title: Async runner choice
sections.what: Tells the async test runner to use asyncio for these tests.
sections.why: Likely reason: the agent code is written for asyncio.

sections.name: step
sections.title: Process step builder
sections.what: Builds a sample process step with a given effort share.
sections.why: Effort shares are what the drift check measures, so tests need to set them directly.

sections.name: drifting
sections.title: Drifting sample output
sections.what: Builds a sample output whose effort shares add up to 0.7, not 1.0.
sections.why: Creates a deliberately inconsistent record that should trigger the drift warning.

sections.name: clean
sections.title: Clean sample output
sections.what: Builds a sample output whose effort shares add up to 1.0.
sections.why: Creates a consistent record that should pass with no warning.

sections.name: suspending
sections.title: Pausing fake client
sections.what: Wraps a fake client so each call pauses a set number of times before answering, like a real network wait.
sections.why: Makes concurrent runs actually take turns, which is the only way the bug can show.
sections.watch_out: The pause counts must vary across tests, or the interleaving cases are not really covered.

sections.name: run_pair
sections.title: Run two agents together
sections.what: Starts two cartographer runs at the same time with their own fake clients and waits for both results.
sections.why: This is the setup that reproduces overlapping runs.

sections.name: test_drift_is_attributed_to_the_run_that_drifted
sections.title: Drift warning stays with its run
sections.what: Checks that only the drifting run keeps its warning and gets a second attempt, while the clean run gets no warning and only one attempt. It runs across several pause combinations.
sections.why: Stops a clean run from paying for another run's retry or losing its own warning.
sections.watch_out: The pause combinations are what expose the interleaving, so removing them weakens the test.

sections.name: test_two_drifting_runs_each_keep_their_own_warning
sections.title: Two drifting runs keep separate warnings
sections.what: Checks that when both runs drift, each one keeps exactly one warning of its own.
sections.why: Catches cases where warnings get merged or swapped between runs.

sections.name: test_no_warning_escapes_the_agent
sections.title: No warning leaks out of the agent
sections.what: Checks that no drift warning reaches the process-wide warning filter when two runs overlap.
sections.why: A warning that reaches the global filter has no owner, which is the bug this file guards.

sections.name: test_an_unrelated_warning_costs_no_retry
sections.title: Unrelated notice costs nothing
sections.what: Checks that a deprecation notice from the SDK passes through to the caller without an extra attempt and without appearing as a soft warning.
sections.why: The module notes that the eval layer treats soft warnings as hard failures, and that an SDK notice is not a defect in the record.
sections.watch_out: The category filter is what stops this notice from triggering a paid retry. If the filter is removed, each such notice costs a full billed call.

summary: Tests that two agent runs happening at the same time do not mix up their warnings or cause extra paid retries.
purpose: Protects against a bug where warnings from one run leak into another run when runs overlap.
why: The module description says the warning capture is global to the whole program. Holding it open across a pause lets a concurrent run's warnings land in the wrong record. Large fan-outs make this likely.
how: Two cartographer runs are started together with fake clients that pause a few times, so they really interleave. Tests then check that a drift warning belongs only to the run that drifted, that each run keeps its own warnings, that no warning escapes the agent, and that an unrelated notice costs no retry.
inputs: Sample process steps with chosen effort shares, fake clients with set pause counts, and a sample brief.
outputs: Pass or fail results for each concurrency case. No real calls are made.
risks: The bug only appears when runs actually interleave. If the fake client stops pausing, these tests can pass while the bug is still there.
debug: If a warning appears on the wrong run, check whether warning capture is held open across an await point. If retries double unexpectedly, check the warning category filter.
